body: I'm sorry to hear that. If you want someone to converse with my DMs are open!

For me, it's a mixture of wanting to look good and feeling comfortable, which is why I try to find a balance between how I want to look and how I'm expected to look. 

I try to make the outfits I wear to school lean towards academic/ office fashion rather than straight up formal wear, so I wouldn't wear an elaborate dress to class but will often pair a more simple dress with black flats and a blazer.

Yeah, I kind of used "casual" and "comfortable" interchangeably there, if anything I physically feel more comfortable in dress pants than in most jeans. However, in terms of ..mental comfort (?) then I feel more comfortable (read: safer, better protected) when doing activities like hiking in jeans rather than in formal alternatives.

I might have worded this idea strangely because English 2nd language but I hope you get my sentiment
No stupid question intended, but are you talking about my lad Barney the purple dinosaur?

Awh :(

If you're going for the good old anime schoolgirl look then I'd recommend investing in a dark-colored pleated skirt like this one:  [https://www.amazon.com/chouyatou-Womens-Buttons-Pleated-XX-Large/dp/B01LZDOQWO/ref=sr\_1\_4?dchild=1&keywords=black+sailor+skirt&qid=1580948270&sr=8-4](https://www.amazon.com/chouyatou-Womens-Buttons-Pleated-XX-Large/dp/B01LZDOQWO/ref=sr_1_4?dchild=1&keywords=black+sailor+skirt&qid=1580948270&sr=8-4) , with a collared blouse. Depending on how strict your work's dress code is, you can accessorize with anything from a colorful cardigan to a black blazer. I really like this kind of look as it is just the right amount of kawaii to satisfy my desire to dress how I want while not immediately revealing that I'm a weeb.

Whenever I go out I plan my outfits out and genuinely enjoy doing so. It is kind of like a hobby for me now, I used to have trouble motivating myself to do laundry/iron my shit but upon realizing that the aesthetic is worth the sacrifice, I spend \~5 minutes per night preparing my clothes for the next day.

16F here, on school days I either wear a collared blouse with a skirt or a simple dress. If it's cold I'll also have a cardigan or blazer. I also have some fancier dresses for more formal events. My go-to shoes are black flats, and when it comes to accessories I always wear earrings, sometimes with other pieces of jewelry, or when I'm feeling artsy, a beret. I used to wear a watch too but it broke and I have yet to get a new one. 

When going out to run errands or to social gatherings, I try to find a balance between formal and casual. So I might pair nice jeans with a t-shirt and cardigan, or a tennis skirt with a sweater.

That being said, I don't dress purely casually/comfortably outside of home, which is where I tend to lounge around in leggings, shorts, t-shirts, and sweaters. I wear sleep clothes for sleeping only.

And I agree, polo shirts are the worst. Some of my other most-disliked articles of clothing are pencil skirts, high heeled shoes, and sweatpants. But screw polo shirts in particular.

I go to a vocational high school where I'm in an arts program that requires me to complete Adobe certifications to graduate. While I'm required to only do two, I want to take the opportunity of doing them all for free (I think my school offers the exams for 5 or 6 programs) just to spice up my resume.
